A regular hexagon with side length 4 is subdivided into a lattice of 96 equilateral triangles of side length 1. Let $S$ be the set of all vertices of this lattice. Compute the number of nondegenerate triangles with vertices in $S$ that contain the center of the hexagon strictly in their interior.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Let \(O\) be the center of the hexagon.

Use lattice coordinates \((x,y,z)\in\mathbb Z^3\) with
\[
x+y+z=0,\qquad |x|,|y|,|z|\le 4.
\]
This models the triangular lattice in the regular hexagon of side length \(4\). The center is \((0,0,0)\), and there are \(60\) noncenter lattice vertices.

Group the noncenter vertices by rays from \(O\). If a primitive direction has maximum coordinate \(m\), then the ray contains \(\lfloor 4/m\rfloor\) lattice points. A direct enumeration of primitive directions gives:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
\text{type} & \#\text{ rays} & \text{points per ray}\\ \hline
A & 6 & 4\\
B & 6 & 2\\
C & 12 & 1\\
D & 12 & 1
\end{array}
\]

These are the directions with \(m=1,2,3,4\), respectively.

By symmetry, in each \(60^\circ\) sector the ray types occur in the order

\[
A,\;D,\;C,\;B,\;C,\;D.
\]

For a fixed point \(P\) on a ray \(r\), let \(s(r)\) be the number of unordered pairs \(\{Q,R\}\) of lattice vertices such that \(O\) is strictly inside \(\triangle PQR\). This depends only on the type of \(r\), not on which point on the ray is chosen.

For a fixed ray \(r\), look at the \(17\) rays in the open semicircle from \(r\) to its opposite ray. If the ray \(a\) is the first of the two other vertices in this semicircle, then the allowable second ray must be the antipode of a ray lying strictly between \(r\) and \(a\). Therefore, if the weights of the \(17\) rays in that semicircle are

\[
x_1,x_2,\dots,x_{17},
\]
then

\[
s(r)=\sum_{i=1}^{17} x_i(x_1+\cdots+x_{i-1}).
\]

For the four ray types, the weight sequences are:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
\text{type} & \text{sequence in the semicircle} & s(r)\\ \hline
A & (1,1,2,1,1,4,1,1,2,1,1,4,1,1,2,1,1) & 310\\
B & (1,1,4,1,1,2,1,1,4,1,1,2,1,1,4,1,1) & 358\\
C & (2,1,1,4,1,1,2,1,1,4,1,1,2,1,1,4,1) & 385\\
D & (1,2,1,1,4,1,1,2,1,1,4,1,1,2,1,1,4) & 385
\end{array}
\]

Each valid triangle is counted once for each of its three vertices, so the desired number is

\[
\frac13\sum_{P\ne O} s(\text{ray of }P).
\]

Thus

\[
\begin{aligned}
N&=\frac13\Big(6\cdot 4\cdot 310
+6\cdot 2\cdot 358
+12\cdot 1\cdot 385
+12\cdot 1\cdot 385\Big)\\
&=\frac13(7440+4296+9240+9240)\\
&=\frac{20976}{3}\\
&=6992.
\end{aligned}
\]

\[
\boxed{6992}
\]
